Playbook.name: Change Audit — Password Reset of a Privileged or Service Account by Another User (4724) - SOC Playbook

Reference.title: MITRE ATT and CK T1098 Account Manipulation
MITRE ATT and CK T1078 Valid Accounts

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: An administrator-initiated password reset (event 4724) was performed against a privileged or service account by another user - the watched set includes svc_*, *_srv, achuser, aml_srv, krbtgt and the named admin accounts (ramiadmin, harethadmin). Unlike a self-service change (4723), a 4724 means one identity reset another account's password. The triage question is whether this is a sanctioned rotation/offboarding by the account's administrator, an automated PAM rotation, or an attacker seizing a high-value account by overwriting its password.
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Resetting a service or privileged account password is a direct account-takeover primitive: the attacker sets a known password and then authenticates as a trusted identity, inheriting its access to core banking systems. A krbtgt reset has domain-wide Kerberos impact, and a service-account reset can break or hijack the workloads that depend on it.

Assets.AssetType: Privileged and service accounts (svc_*, *_srv, achuser, aml_srv, krbtgt, named admins)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Account Management auditing shipped to logs-system.security-* with 4724 present (verified live: ~3.5k 4724 events in 30 days).
winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName (actor) and winlog.event_data.TargetUserName (account reset) populated (verified live).

Signal.Name: Privileged reset by another user
Signal.Details: event.code 4724 where TargetUserName is a privileged/service account and SubjectUserName is a different identity.

Signal.Name: Reset-then-use
Signal.Details: The reset account authenticating (4624/4768/4769) shortly after the reset, indicating the new password is in use.

Input.name: $target_user
Input.description: Privileged/service account whose password was reset (winlog.event_data.TargetUserName from the alert).

Input.name: $actor
Input.description: User who performed the reset (winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName from the alert).

Input.name: $host
Input.description: Host/DC that recorded the reset (host.name from the alert).

ImmediateCapture.Item: Confirm actor is different from target (a genuine by-another-user reset, not a self change)
Whether a change ticket / rotation schedule covers this reset

InitialAssessment.Rule: If $actor is the documented owner/administrator of $target_user or the known PAM rotation identity, and a ticket or schedule covers it, lean False Positive / Misconfiguration - but still verify the account was not used abnormally afterwards.

If $actor is not an expected administrator of the account, if krbtgt or a named admin is the target without a planned change, or if the account is used immediately after, escalate as potential account takeover.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the 4724 reset of $target_user by $actor was a sanctioned change or an account takeover, and whether the account was used after the reset.

Step.name: Confirm the reset event and its actor
Step.Purpose: Pin down who reset the account, when and where, and whether related account changes accompanied it (4738 attribute change).
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND event.code IN ("4724","4723","4738") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events=COUNT(*), first_seen=MIN(@timestamp), last_seen=MAX(@timestamp), actors=VALUES(winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName), hosts=VALUES(host.name) BY event.code, event.action | SORT event.code ASC | LIMIT 50
Step.AnalystNotes: Confirm the actor differs from the target (by-another-user reset). A 4738 attribute change alongside the reset (e.g. UAC flags cleared) strengthens a takeover hypothesis. A single reset by the account's known admin is routine.

Step.name: Measure the actor's reset breadth
Step.Purpose: One reset under a ticket is routine; one actor resetting several privileged/service accounts in the window is a takeover spree.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$actor" AND event.code == "4724" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS resets=COUNT(*), targets=COUNT_DISTINCT(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName), touched=VALUES(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName), hosts=VALUES(host.name) BY winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: A PAM/rotation identity resetting many service accounts on schedule is Misconfiguration/authorised; a human or unexpected actor resetting multiple privileged accounts is a strong escalate signal.

Step.name: Check whether the reset account was used afterwards
Step.Purpose: The purpose of overwriting a service/privileged password is to log in as it. Authentication by $target_user after the reset is the key takeover signal.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND event.code IN ("4624","4768","4769") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS logons=COUNT(*), first_seen=MIN(@timestamp), last_seen=MAX(@timestamp), types=VALUES(winlog.event_data.LogonType), src=VALUES(source.ip), hosts=VALUES(host.name) BY event.code | SORT event.code ASC | LIMIT 50
Step.AnalystNotes: Correlate first_seen here against the reset time in INV-01. A logon from an unexpected source or an interactive/remote-interactive logon by a service account shortly after the reset indicates the credential is now attacker-controlled.

Step.name: Look for concurrent manipulation by the actor
Step.Purpose: A reset combined with account creation, enabling, or privileged-group additions by the same actor is takeover-and-persist, not maintenance.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName == "$actor" AND event.code IN ("4720","4722","4728","4732","4756","4726","4725") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS actions=COUNT(*), codes=VALUES(event.code), targets=VALUES(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName), members=VALUES(winlog.event_data.MemberName), hosts=VALUES(host.name) BY winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: Group additions (4728/4732/4756) or new accounts (4720/4722) by the same actor around the reset indicate an active takeover chain. members shows any account the actor added to a group in the window.

Node.Condition: INV-03 shows $target_user authenticating after the reset (especially from an unexpected source), OR INV-04 shows the same actor performing group additions/account creation, AND no change record covers the reset.
Node.Result: True Positive (account takeover / persistence - escalate to IR immediately)

Node.Condition: INV-01/INV-02 show the reset performed by an actor who is not an expected administrator of the account, or a krbtgt / named-admin reset with no planned change, even without post-reset use yet.
Node.Result: Needs Escalation (unauthorised-looking privileged reset - confirm with the account owner before closing)

Node.Condition: The reset was performed by the documented administrator/service-desk owner of the account under a matching change ticket (rotation, offboarding, incident remediation) and INV-03 shows no abnormal use.
An automated PAM/password-rotation identity resets service-account passwords on a schedule and trips the rule as recurring noise.
Node.Result: Misconfiguration (tune the rule for the PAM actor; do not broadly exception privileged targets)

Node.Condition: Actor cannot be attributed as an authorised administrator, or evidence is mixed.

FalsePositive.Definition: An authorised administrator or the account owner reset the password under an approved change - a sanctioned and attributable action, not a benign assumption.

Indicators.Item: $actor is the documented administrator/owner of $target_user and is named on a change ticket covering the window.
Reset is a single event consistent with rotation/offboarding/remediation.
INV-03 shows no abnormal authentication by the account afterwards.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the change ticket / rotation request reference with the owning team.
Close as false_positive with the reference attached.

TruePositive.Definition: An attacker overwrote a privileged/service account password to seize the identity and use its access.

Indicators.Item: Reset by an actor who is not an expected administrator of the account, with no change record.
Reset-then-use: the account authenticates after the reset (INV-03), especially from an unexpected source or logon type.
Concurrent account manipulation by the same actor - group additions or new accounts (INV-04); krbtgt reset outside planned remediation.

SOCAction.Item: Re-reset $target_user to an admin-controlled password and revoke its sessions/tickets.
Disable or reset $actor if compromise is suspected; reverse any group additions from INV-04.
Open an incident; if krbtgt was reset abnormally, engage IR for domain Kerberos assessment.

Misconfiguration.Definition: An automated PAM/rotation tool resets service-account passwords by design and generates recurring 4724 alerts.

Indicators.Item: Same rotation identity resetting a consistent set of service accounts on a fixed cadence.
No human actor, no post-reset abnormal use, no concurrent elevation.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the rotation tool and its service identity with the platform team.
Tune the rule to exclude the PAM actor for the managed accounts only; track under detection-tuning.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: If takeover is indicated (INV-03/INV-04), re-reset $target_user under admin control and revoke its active sessions/tickets.
Freeze $actor and any accounts it created or elevated in the window.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Reverse unauthorised group memberships; audit everything the reset account and the actor touched.
If $actor is compromised, reset it and forensic-triage the host from INV-01.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Review who holds reset rights over privileged/service accounts; move service-account credentials under PAM with checkout logging.
Alert on reset-then-authenticate sequences for the watched account set within N minutes.

Escalation.Trigger: Any reset-then-use of the account, concurrent account manipulation by the actor, a krbtgt/named-admin reset without a planned change, or a reset by an unattributable actor.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Change ticket / rotation schedule verified and matches actor, target and window.
INV-03 confirms no abnormal authentication by the account after the reset.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Account re-reset under admin control, sessions/tickets revoked, group changes reversed.
Actor status resolved (compromise vs insider) and root cause documented.
